name: Wilmington
reason: Own flindersandoutback town page names a heritage walking trail and Hancocks Lookout on Horrocks Pass Road; one counted source and a short stop (rule 1 marginal).
objection: A small farming town whose sights are a short heritage trail and a roadside lookout; a visitor passing through gets under an hour.

name: Gladstone
reason: Flindersandoutback town page names the heritage-listed Gladstone Gaol (internment camp, tour) and the Southern Flinders Discovery Centre: a half-hour-plus visit (rule 2).
objection: Small town and a single counted source; the gaol's opening is limited, so it could be only a drive-through.

name: Crystal Brook
reason: Only listed by name among the region's towns; no source names anything to see or do (rule 1/2).
objection: It is a Mid North highway stop where visitors do pass through; a guide might yet name a mural or museum.

name: Spalding
reason: Named only as the southern edge of the region; no source names a thing to see (rule 1/2).
objection: It is the southern gateway and some visitors stop for a bakery or the Broughton River.

name: Wilpena Pound Resort
reason: Accommodation and visitor centre, a business; the place is Wilpena Pound/Ikara-Flinders Ranges NP (rule 2, vehicle/operator not a spot).
objection: The only base in the park and the visitor centre; people do stop here. But it duplicates the Pound as a place.

name: Leigh Creek
reason: Town with its own flindersandoutback page and Wikivoyage coverage as the gateway to the northern Flinders; three counted sources (rule 1, town rule).
objection: A purpose-built mining service town with little to see; the proposer may fold it into another spot.

name: Lyndhurst
reason: Has its own Wikivoyage page with See listings (Talc Alf art works, Ochre Pits, Ochre Cliffs) at the Strzelecki/Oodnadatta junction (rule 1, town rule).
objection: Hamlet of a few dozen; sights are small and one counted source.

name: Copley
reason: Wikivoyage lists a cafe and information stop only; nothing to see or do (rule 2, shop/cafe).
objection: Quandong Cafe is a known roadside stop for travellers.

name: Nepabunna
reason: Community; the only draw is Iga Warta cultural tours, an operator, and visitor access is by arrangement (rule 2, operator).
objection: An Adnyamathanha cultural experience a guide promotes; the operator's place could qualify with a second source.

name: Balcanoona
reason: Park headquarters and shearers quarters accommodation, not a sight (rule 2).
objection: It is the access point for the Gammon Ranges and has a heritage shearers' quarters.

name: Bunyeroo Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au (two counted) name the gorge and its scenic drive to Razorback; a second-tier stop that guides single out (rules 1-3).
objection: It is a gravel drive within a park already likely listed; lookouts on it are folded in here.

name: Arkaroo Rock
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name the 6,000-year-old Adnyamathanha rock art and its trail (rules 1-2).
objection: A short walk with a small art panel; only an hour at most.

name: Arkaroo Rock Walk
reason: Duplicate of Arkaroo Rock (the walk is how one reaches the art).
objection: The trail is a distinct activity for hikers.

name: Cazneaux Tree
reason: Wikivoyage itself says 'nothing so special about this tree'; a roadside tree is a ten-minute photo stop (rule 3).
objection: A named photographic landmark in the Flinders photographic tradition.

name: Sacred Canyon
reason: Wikivoyage and flindersandoutback (two counted) name the Adnyamathanha engravings in the canyon, with guided tours from the resort (rules 1-2).
objection: Remote 13.5 km gravel road; the site is sacred and visits are restricted to marked areas.

name: Old Wilpena Station
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name the station precinct with interpretive signs (and Hills Homestead) (rules 1-2).
objection: Little remains of the original buildings; may be only an hour's detour.

name: Rawnsley Bluff
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name it, but as a bluff/lookout on the Pound's eastern side; Wikivoyage text I opened lists only the Rawnsley Lookout, so a walk to the bluff is a hike rather than a stand-alone stop.
objection: For: a headline eastern view of Wilpena Pound with two counted sources. Against: part of Ikara-Flinders Ranges NP's walks.

name: Rawnsley Lookout
reason: 170 m walk to an information lookout on the Flinders Ranges Way; a short pull-out (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it by name with fossil information.

name: Hucks Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names it: a roadside lookout with carpark and picnic area over ancient sediments; one counted source, a short stop (rule 3 marginal).
objection: For: easy, named by Wikivoyage and on the main road. Against: a short pull-out, 'part of' the Pound walk per the script.

name: Wangara Lookout
reason: Part of the Wilpena Pound hike (7 km walk to a lookout); a feature of the track, not a separate spot (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as its own lookout with a notable view of the Pound.

name: Razorback Lookout
reason: Lookout on the Bunyeroo Gorge drive; kept inside Bunyeroo Gorge (rule 3, part of a larger spot).
objection: Wikivoyage promotes the famous Razorback photo of the track into the Pound.

name: Brachina Lookout
reason: Midway stop on the Brachina Gorge geological trail; part of Brachina Gorge (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it an excellent stop.

name: Wilpena Pound Solar Panel Lookout
reason: A lookout over a solar farm beside the resort; minor and not a draw (rule 3).
objection: A short walk with the Living with Land signage near the resort.

name: Living with Land Walk
reason: 1 km interpretive stroll at the resort; one source, minor and a near-duplicate of the resort precinct (rule 3).
objection: Interprets Adnyamathanha and settler life, which is cultural content.

name: Hills Homestead Walk
reason: Wikivoyage: 6.6 km, two hours return from the resort to preserved pioneering sites; one counted source.
objection: For: a 2-hour heritage walk. Against: overlaps Old Wilpena Station/Hills Homestead and is one walk of many in the park.

name: Wilpena Pound Trail (Inside the Pound)
reason: Duplicate of Wilpena Pound (the trail is inside the feature itself) (rule 3).
objection: A 7.9 km walk is a major activity of the park.

name: Trezona Hike
reason: Wikivoyage: 8 km, four-hour walk through the Heysen Range past Ediacaran Trezona Formation and the Ediacaran Golden Spike; one counted source.
objection: For: only Southern Hemisphere golden spike, a geological draw. Against: a single hike among many, the spike is already a separate Wikivoyage item.

name: Boom and Bust Hike
reason: 2 km easy loop near the visitor centre; minor and one source (rule 3).
objection: Easy and near the resort, so a convenient half-hour walk.

name: Chambers Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage names the petroglyphs as the chief attraction and the gorge as a campground; a second-tier stop (rule 1-2).
objection: Remote 4WD-condition track; one counted source.

name: Aroona Ruins
reason: flindersandoutback names scenic ruins and kayaking on Aroona Dam near Leigh Creek; one counted source.
objection: For: a second-tier heritage and water stop. Against: only a blog mention, and ruins are modest.

name: Akurra Trail
reason: A guided cultural tour (operator), not a place (rule: tour/operator).
objection: Adnyamathanha-guided tours of a notable ecosystem near Leigh Creek.

name: Blinman Pools
reason: flindersandoutback names the hike from Parachilna to the Blinman Pools as an outback oasis; one counted source.
objection: For: a real swimming/walk destination. Against: for experienced hikers only and reached by a long walk with no visitor page.

name: Blinman Heritage Mine
reason: southaustralia.com and the flindersandoutback listing (two counted) name the guided historic copper mine tour (rules 1-2).
objection: A small tour that may be run at set times.

name: Parachilna Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage describes the scenic gorge drive between Blinman and Parachilna with free camping, and flindersandoutback lists it (rule 1); second-tier scenic stop.
objection: Mainly a road through a gorge.

name: Prairie Hotel
reason: Famous Parachilna pub (feral food), with three counted sources; a business but a recognised landmark.
objection: For: an outback icon people stop for. Against: it is a pub/accommodation (rule 2 excludes venues that are only restaurants).

name: Southern Flinders Rail Trail
reason: flindersandoutback names the rail trail for cyclists; one counted source.
objection: For: a recreation trail. Against: no detail on the route and a bare list mention.

name: Heritage Rail Trail (Broken Hill to Port Pirie)
reason: A 395 km touring route through 14 towns, not a place (spot is a place).
objection: A promoted route with its own marketing.

name: Bridal Track
reason: One list mention of a 4WD track with no visitor detail; access is via private stations (rule 1/2).
objection: Named by the regional board as the one track to try.

name: Arkaba Walk
reason: A four-night guided luxury walk run by an operator on a private station (operator, rule 2).
objection: A Great Walk of Australia.

name: Elder Range (Merna Mora)
reason: 4WD track accessible only from a private station; a list mention (rule 2).
objection: Named as a top-rated track.

name: Caernarvon Track
reason: flindersandoutback has a listing page and a signature-experiences mention: a top-rated 4WD track; two counted sources.
objection: For: two counted sources. Against: a track with permitted-area restrictions that most visitors cannot drive.

name: Mount Jacob Back Track
reason: One list mention among 4WD tracks; no detail and access via private land (rule 1/2).
objection: Called a top-rated track.

name: Wadna Aboriginal Culture Tours
reason: An operator, not a place (rule: tour/operator).
objection: Two counted sources name it.

name: Ediacara Conservation Park
reason: Wikivoyage names the Ediacara fossil site (Dickinsonia); the site is accessed through guided tours at Nilpena Station, so open access is arguable; one counted source.
objection: For: a world-class fossil site on a World Heritage tentative list. Against: visits are mostly operator tours.

name: Italowie Gorge
reason: The parks.sa.gov.au Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges page names the Italowie Gorge hike past Mount McKinlay Spring with a campground (rule 1, managing agency).
objection: Remote; one counted source and a long hike.

name: Weetootla Gorge
reason: The parks.sa.gov.au page names the Weetootla Gorge hike and campground (rule 1, managing agency).
objection: Remote 4WD-area hike; one counted source.

name: Lake Frome
reason: parks.sa.gov.au names it as a unique feature of the Gammon Ranges (100 km salt lake); 4WD edge access; one counted source.
objection: For: dramatic salt lake. Against: no developed visitor site and the Plains Block is a traditional hunting ground.

name: Arkaroola Observatories
reason: Two counted sources (flindersandoutback) name the public observatories in an International Dark Sky Sanctuary; Wikivoyage mentions the astronomy tours (rule 1-2).
objection: Visits are by guided night tour at the resort.

name: Arkaroola Ridgetop Tour
reason: A guided 4WD tour, an operator product; the place is Arkaroola/Sillers Lookout (spot is a place).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it world famous.

name: Mawson Plateau
reason: Only reached via the Arkaroola ridgetop tour; a tour destination, no open public access of its own (rule 2).
objection: A distinct geological plateau with its own Wikipedia article.

name: Talc Alf Art Works
reason: Wikivoyage lists the sculptures at Lyndhurst as its first See item; one counted source and a short visit.
objection: For: quirky roadside art that travellers stop for. Against: no description, and may be a private gallery.

name: Ochre Cliffs
reason: Wikivoyage names the cliffs 50 km north of Lyndhurst and their Aboriginal use; one counted source.
objection: For: coloured cliffs and cultural meeting place. Against: remote and little visitor information.

name: Ochre Pits (Lyndhurst)
reason: Wikivoyage names the Ochre Pits 2 km north of Lyndhurst, with Aboriginal significance; one counted source, a short stop.
objection: For: easy access. Against: a short stop, same cultural theme as the Ochre Cliffs, and many visitors miss the turnoff.

name: Camel Treks Australia (Beltana)
reason: Tour operator, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place); Beltana itself is judged separately.
objection: Camel rides are a draw, but they are the operator's product.

name: Beltana Station
reason: Wikivoyage describes Beltana as a historic township worth a couple of hours' poking about; one counted source, a short-to-medium visit.
objection: For: heritage ghost-town on the Outback road, guide-named. Against: one source, station is partly private, plain flat setting.

name: Giant Gum Tree
reason: Flinders and Outback tourism and southaustralia.com name the 500-year-old Giant Red Gum at Orroroo a 'must-see'; free roadside tree icon (second-tier quirky landmark).
objection: A single tree is a short stop (10-20 min) and Orroroo is out of the way.

name: Yacca Lookout Trail
reason: Source says it is a privately marked trail for guests of Skytrek Willow Springs Station only: not open to the public.
objection: southaustralia.com also lists it, but access is for guests.

name: Death Rock
reason: Duplicate of Death Rock and Kanyaka Waterhole (the listing covers rock and waterhole as one 10-minute walk); a short pull-out stop, no separate draw.
objection: The agency names it, and a one-hour Kanyaka Station ruins visit nearby may justify a combined spot judged elsewhere.

name: Proby's Grave
reason: Minor grave/memorial of an explorer (COVERAGE rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as a See entry.

name: Itali Itali
reason: Single Wikivoyage mention of an Aboriginal place near Quorn with no visitor facilities or interpretation; sensitive site, nothing to do for half an hour.
objection: Cultural significance may be real, but no source gives public access.

name: Quorn Silo Light Show
reason: Nightly projected show: a recurring show, not a place (rule 4).
objection: It runs nightly so it is nearly always there, but it is an event, not a permanent sight.

name: Dutchmans Stern
reason: Parks SA page for Dutchmans Stern Conservation Park: summit hike with Flinders views north of Quorn; open (4WD-only entry road after storm damage, and a short closure 31 Oct-6 Nov for pest control).
objection: Hard walk, access road currently limited, 484 views.

name: Mount Brown Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA page: 964 m peak with lookout and loop walk, one of the highest Southern Flinders peaks; keep as the park (Mount Brown is the same place).
objection: One source only; temporary closures for pest control.

name: Mount Brown
reason: duplicate of Mount Brown Conservation Park (the peak is the park's summit walk).
objection: The summit is the draw; but the same page covers both.

name: Quorn Bush Food Walking Trail
reason: Duplicate of Pithi Kawi Bush Food Garden / Quorn Native Flora Reserve walk: a short, easy 2 km town walk, no distinct draw.
objection: Two counted sources list it.

name: Pithi Kawi Bush Food Garden
reason: Small town garden, one source, minor; folded with the Quorn native flora walk.
objection: Aboriginal bush-food interpretation is interesting but it is a roadside garden.

name: Argadells
reason: Historic homestead run as accommodation/farm stay: a business (accommodation).
objection: Heritage homestead mentioned in an itinerary.

name: Waukarie Falls
reason: Parks SA (Mount Brown CP) and the tourism listing name Waukarie Creek/Falls; the listing is a 5.8 km, 3 hour linear Heysen Trail walk, and the falls flow only after rain.
objection: For: two counted sources, a real walk. Against: seasonal falls, linear walk needing a car shuttle, part of Mount Brown/Heysen area.

name: Willochra Plain
reason: A broad plain seen from lookouts, no place to go (rule 3: part of the lookout views).
objection: Scenic, but not a distinct visitable place.

name: Mambray Creek Campground
reason: Campground/trailhead inside Mount Remarkable NP: accommodation and part of the larger park, not a distinct draw.
objection: Gateway to the park's walks.

name: Willowie trails (Mount Remarkable)
reason: Mountain-bike trail network inside Mount Remarkable NP: part of the larger park and duplicate of Remarkable Epic Trail.
objection: Two sources; cycling is a real activity.

name: Remarkable Epic Trail
reason: Mountain-bike trail inside Mount Remarkable NP, part of the park listing; one source.
objection: Long trail could be a hike-category spot, but the park covers it.

name: Telowie Gorge Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA and Flinders and Outback tourism both name the gorge (part of Wapma Thura-Southern Flinders Ranges NP): walks, wildlife, creek flows in winter.
objection: Parks SA notes it now forms part of Wapma Thura NP, so it may duplicate a larger park spot.

name: Hancock's Lookout
reason: Regional page singles out Mount Ellen and Hancock's lookouts for Flinders views; one source, a short stop.
objection: For: guide-named viewpoint. Against: one source, 10-minute pull-out.

name: Mount Ellen Lookout
reason: Regional page singles out Mount Ellen and Hancock's lookouts for views; one source, a short stop.
objection: For: guide-named viewpoint. Against: one source, short roadside stop, likely near-duplicate of Hancock's.

name: The Bluff Lookout (Port Germein)
reason: Pull-out lookout to view Port Germein Jetty; part of the jetty visit (rule 3).
objection: Regional page names it for jetty views.

name: Port Germein Jetty
reason: Wikivoyage Port Germein and the Southern Flinders regional page name the 1.6 km jetty, the longest wooden jetty in SA; a walk, crabbing and fishing.
objection: Exposed at low tide and a single structure; the town has little else.

name: Port Germein Tide Clock
reason: Minor monument on the foreshore (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Nyrstar Port Pirie Smelter
reason: Working industrial site with no public access; exterior only.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as a see entry.

name: Flinders View Park
reason: Ordinary town park, one source, no distinct draw.
objection: Wikivoyage lists a view.

name: Solomontown Beach
reason: Wikivoyage names the Port Pirie beach for swimming; a town beach with one counted source.
objection: For: second-tier beach. Against: one source, ordinary suburban beach on an industrial gulf shore.

name: Port Pirie National Trust Museum
reason: Regional page names it with Melrose and Steamtown as a heritage highlight; museum is open to the public (in the historic railway station area).
objection: For: counted tourism source, museum. Against: one source, opening times limited, hours of interest unclear.

name: Port Pirie Regional Art Gallery
reason: Small regional gallery, one source, no notable collection named.
objection: Open to the public, but nothing singled out.

name: Port Pirie Mural Trail
reason: Street-art listing in a town, one source; folded into the town's visit.
objection: Murals are free and always there.

name: Port Pirie Heritage Trail
reason: Town heritage trail of buildings seen from the street, one source.
objection: A guide's walking route can qualify, but exteriors only.

name: Port Augusta Water Tower Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage and the Flinders and Outback listing both name the 1882 tower with a balcony view over Spencer Gulf and the Flinders; two counted sources.
objection: Short stop and opening limited; Port Augusta West suburb.

name: Port Augusta Wharf Precinct
reason: Wikivoyage describes the former wharf as a recreational precinct, partly hidden behind a supermarket; one source.
objection: For: waterfront walk, guide-named. Against: obscured, ordinary promenade.

name: Blanche Harbor
reason: Wikivoyage: rehabilitated coast, picnic and birdwatching 23 km out on Shack Road; one source.
objection: For: guide-named nature spot. Against: one source, remote track, little to do.

name: Port Augusta Foreshore
reason: Generic swim spot beside the town, one source, no distinct draw.
objection: Swimming is possible.

name: Port Augusta Heritage Walk
reason: Town heritage walk of exteriors, one blog source.
objection: A guide's walking route can qualify but no stops named.

name: Town Carriage Museum (Peterborough)
reason: Wikivoyage lists it and the 4-day itinerary names it with Steamtown; open museum of railway carriages.
objection: For: two counted sources. Against: small, likely overlaps Steamtown rail-heritage visit.

name: Peterborough Historic Letterpress Print Shop
reason: Tourism listing: volunteer-run tours of a working historic print shop; the itinerary names it (Peterborough Printing Works).
objection: Small volunteer venue, opening limited.

name: Booleroo Steam and Traction Preservation Society
reason: Viewing by appointment only: not reliably open to the public.
objection: The itinerary calls the collection very impressive.

name: Jacka Brothers Brewery
reason: Brewery/cellar door: a business, singled out only as a pit stop with a view (venue rule).
objection: Itinerary says 'you must visit' for the backdrop, so a reviewer might keep.

name: Little Blessings Brewery
reason: Craft brewery and gin business in Laura; a venue, not a destination in its own right.
objection: Two sources list it.

name: The Laura Emporium Gallery and Museum
reason: Mainly an antique shop and cafe with a small machinery museum behind: shop/cafe.
objection: A museum of rural machinery sits at the rear.

name: C.J. Dennis Statue (Laura)
reason: Public sculpture on the main street, a minor stop under 10 minutes (rule 3).
objection: Regional page names it as a feature.

name: Melrose Courthouse Heritage and Interpretive Centre
reason: Tourism listing: Melrose Heritage Museum with five buildings, audio-visual displays on 1848 settlement, Goyder's Line and the Nukunu people; regional page highlights it.
objection: Small town museum with limited hours.

name: Bartagunyah Estate
reason: One of many cellar doors, not singled out as a destination in its own right.
objection: Two itinerary sources; foothill setting.

name: Bundaleer Wines
reason: Cellar door in a hotel; one of many cellar doors.
objection: Award-winning per itinerary.

name: Glenholme Vineyards (Blesing's Garden)
reason: Cellar door; one of many; one source.
objection: Garden setting.

name: The Old Survey Art Gallery
reason: Small private gallery, one blog mention, no notable draw.
objection: Open for art browsing.

name: Stone Hut Aviary
reason: Small private aviary, one blog mention.
objection: Families may enjoy it.

name: Stone Hut Bakery
reason: Bakery: a shop/food business.
objection: Famed pies.

name: Kupsch Bakery
reason: Bakery: a shop/food business.
objection: Popular stop.

name: Wirrabara Silo Art
reason: The itinerary names the stunning silo art at Wirrabara; roadside art icon with one counted source, a short stop.
objection: For: free always-there roadside icon. Against: one source, 10-minute look, silo art is common in SA.

name: Wirrabara Producers Market
reason: Rule 4: a periodic producers market, not there whenever a visitor arrives.
objection: A genuine producers-only market a tourism board lists, but it runs on set days only.

name: Bundaleer Forest
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough); reservoir reserve 40 min from Clare. Counted source (flindersandoutback listing) opened: loop walk, kayak, fishing, picnic, open daily.
objection: Strong second-tier stop with two counted sources; if the proposer places Jamestown area under Flinders it should be kept.

name: Beetaloo Reservoir
reason: Rule 1-3: reservoir precinct near Port Pirie, two counted sources (flindersandoutback region page and listing, opened): open to the public for birdwatching, picnics, barbecues, fishing with permit.
objection: Ordinary water reserve; only half an hour of picnic and a look, and fishing permit needed.

name: Bendleby Ranges
reason: Rule 2: a working station stay with private 4WD and bike trails; the draw is accommodation, not a public place to visit.
objection: Source lists 180 km of trails and a regional blog names it, so day access could exist.

name: Horseshoe Top End
reason: Rule 1/2: a 4WD track named only in passing in a list of 4WD options; no visitor page describing it.
objection: May be a genuine 4WD route a local guide would recommend.

name: Jarvis Hill Lookout and Walking Trail
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) calls it a popular lookout 7 km west of Hawker with views to Wilpena Pound and the ranges. Against: one source, dirt road unsuitable when wet, short visit.
objection: Hawker already has Castle Rock and Camel Hump lookouts; near-duplicate stops.

name: Camel Hump Lookout Walk
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) describes an easy short climb 2 km south of Hawker with panoramic views, good for photographers. Against: one source, a short town-edge walk.
objection: Minor town-edge lookout, near-duplicate of Castle Rock and Jarvis Hill.

name: Castle Rock Walk and Lookout
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) names a prominent castle-shaped rock 2 km east of Hawker with a walking track and a late-light photo draw. Against: one source, short visit.
objection: Local landmark mostly for Hawker residents; one of three overlapping Hawker lookouts.

name: Devil's Peak Walking Trail
reason: Rule 2: the listing (opened) says it is on private property, 1.3 km each way, and gives no location or access, so cannot be treated as open to the public.
objection: It is a promoted walking trail with a 2-hour return time.

name: Ferguson Gorge Scenic Drive and Bush Walk
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) describes a scenic drive through Hannigans Gap and a 1.6 km walk to a gorge with rock pools and yellow-footed rock-wallabies, open to day visitors (4-5 hours). Against: private Moolooloo Station, pay at the homestead, one source.
objection: Operator-run on a station with accommodation; access is by payment to a business.

name: Magnetic Hill
reason: Rule 3 quirky roadside icon: counted listing (opened) calls it a quirky, well-known attraction near Orroroo where vehicles seem to roll uphill, a highlight of a 44 km self-drive loop.
objection: A ten-minute optical illusion on a dirt road, one source.

name: Louden Brae School
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). Also a small restored schoolhouse (listing opened) with only the R.M. Williams link.
objection: Counted tourism listing names it as a historic site.

name: Old Timers Mine
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-outback (Old Timers Mine is in Coober Pedy). Also an operator.
objection: A genuine Coober Pedy attraction; should be kept under the outback region.

name: Red Bridge
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) presents the 1882 Red Bridge over Pekina Creek as a surviving railway landmark in Orroroo. Against: one source, a short look at a bridge.
objection: A minor heritage bridge on a town creek that most visitors would pass.

name: Early Settlers Cottage (Solly's Hut)
reason: Rule 2: open by appointment only (listing opened), a small local museum cottage; not there whenever one arrives.
objection: Counted listing names it, and a visit can run as long as one likes.

name: Diggers Walk Belalie Creek
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). A creek heritage trail with WWI interpretive displays (listing opened).
objection: Interesting walk with Hubert Wilkins story; one counted source.

name: Living in the Rangelands Trail
reason: Rule 2: a privately marked trail for guests of Skytrek Willow Springs Station only (listing opened).
objection: 12 km trail with a tourism listing.

name: Reedy Creek Trail
reason: Rule 2: a privately marked trail for Skytrek Willow Springs Station guests only (listing opened).
objection: 7.4 km trail with a tourism listing.

name: Orroroo Magpie Trail
reason: Rule 3: a geocaching trail through Orroroo town; not a distinct place, town-level activity with only passing counted mentions.
objection: Two counted sources mention it.

name: Jamestown Mural Walk and Outdoor Gallery
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). A town mural walk with a festival outdoor gallery (listing opened).
objection: Two-part mural walk a guide lists.

name: Jamestown Railway Station Museum
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). A railway station museum in Jamestown (listing opened).
objection: Counted listing describes interesting displays.

name: R.M. Williams Story (Jamestown)
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). An outdoor interpretive display in Robinson Park, Jamestown (listing opened).
objection: R.M. Williams is an Australian icon.

name: Fred Teague's Museum
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) describes a compact open museum at Hawker Motors with gemstones, minerals and fossils from the ranges and Waukaringa. Against: one source, a private collection in a service station.
objection: A small private collection inside a motors garage, mostly a stop for Hawker passers-by.

name: R J Finlayson Butter Factory
reason: Rule 2/3: listing (opened) says the building is empty and only a stop on the Gladstone Heritage Walk.
objection: A tourism listing exists for it.

name: Walloway Train Memorial
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial plaque site to a 1901 train collision (listing opened).
objection: Counted listing frames it as a place of reflection 10 km from Orroroo.

name: Aboriginal Carvings
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) names Pekina Creek Aboriginal rock carvings as a short walk from Orroroo main street, a significant cultural heritage site. Against: one source, a short visit, few details of access.
objection: Engraving sites need cultural sensitivity and may be hard for visitors to find without a guide.

name: Hawker Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 3: a town self-guided heritage walk that is part of Hawker itself (duplicate of the town); the listing (opened) only points to a guide brochure.
objection: Two counted sources name it.

name: Adnyamathanha Dreaming Hawker Mural Walking Trail
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) is a self-guided mural walk of Adnyamathanha Dreaming stories by Juanella McKenzie with dual-language labels. Against: one source, a town street-art trail.
objection: Overlaps a town stop and is a street walk rather than a place.

name: Jeff Morgan Gallery (Hawker)
reason: Rule 2: a private gallery/shop named only in an itinerary blog.
objection: Murals mentioned.

name: Flinders Food Co (Hawker)
reason: Rule 2: a cafe, named only in an itinerary blog.
objection: Local food stop in a remote town.

name: Cradock Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 1/3: Cradock Heritage Walk named only in a blog list; a walk through a tiny settlement, no visitor page.
objection: Cradock is a historic ghost-town stop on the Outback route.

name: Aroona Dam
reason: Rule 1-3: counted Leigh Creek town page (opened) describes Aroona Dam Sanctuary with fishing, views, picnic and a 5.5 km interpretive walk; the regional blog also names it for kayaking (open to non-motorised craft).
objection: A modest dam; one town-page paragraph and a blog.

name: Ajax Mine Fossil Reef
reason: Rule 2: a heritage-listed fossil site on the Puttapa pastoral lease; searches found no public access or visitor page, access only on guided tours.
objection: Internationally significant Cambrian fossil site that is part of the Flinders Ranges World Heritage bid.

name: Buckaringa Sanctuary
reason: Rule 1: no counted visitor source found after searching (AWC sanctuary page returned 404; only Wikipedia and non-counted ExplorOz). UNRESOLVED if AWC page exists.
objection: AWC sanctuary with a public scenic drive and lookout and a yellow-footed rock-wallaby colony; may deserve review if a counted source turns up.

name: Bunkers Conservation Reserve
reason: Rule 3: private conservation reserve whose visitor draw is the Caernarvon Track, listed separately; duplicate of that track.
objection: The reserve manager takes visitors for camping.

name: Horrocks Pass
reason: Case for: the counted Wilmington town page (opened) points to Horrocks Pass Road and Hancocks Lookout with views to Spencer Gulf; the pass has a Horrocks monument and lookout. Against: one passing mention, the lookout is the real stop.
objection: Scenic road and a monument; Hancocks Lookout may be the actual spot and the pass a drive.

name: Kanalla Falls
reason: Rule 1: no counted source; a waterfall inside Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park (part of a larger spot), seasonal flow.
objection: Wikipedia article exists and it is a named feature.

name: Mount Serle
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; a peak on a pastoral station.
objection: Historic Eyre landmark.

name: Mount Hack
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; the summit sits in the private Warraweena conservation reserve.
objection: Highest point of the reserve.

name: Mount Gee
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; a remote peak in the Arkaroola area.
objection: Wikipedia-only.

name: Baroota Dam
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; a water reservoir with no visitor page.
objection: Reservoir beside Mount Remarkable National Park.

name: Warratyi
reason: Rule 2: an archaeological rock shelter with no public access and no visitor source.
objection: Globally significant site.

name: Moolawatana Station
reason: Rule 2: a pastoral station; no counted source and no public visit.
objection: Historic station.

name: Wooltana Station
reason: Rule 2: a pastoral station; no counted source and no public visit.
objection: Historic station.

name: Willochra Creek
reason: Rule 1/3: a creek; no counted source.
objection: Wikipedia-only.

name: Rawnsley Park Heli-Camping
reason: Operators rule: a heli-camping experience from a station, a business rather than a place.
objection: Named in the regional nature blog.

name: Flinders Ranges Self-Drive Loop
reason: Rule 3: a touring route/brochure (listing opened) rather than a place; the stops are separate candidates.
objection: Counted source names it.

name: The Outback Loop
reason: Rule 3: a multi-track touring region (Birdsville, Strzelecki, Oodnadatta tracks; listing opened) rather than a place; belongs mostly to sa-outback.
objection: Two counted sources name it.

name: Quorn Historic Building Walk
reason: Rule 3: a self-guided brochure walk that is part of Quorn town (duplicate of the town); listing opened.
objection: Counted listing names it.

name: Powell Gardens
reason: Rule 3: a small native garden in Quorn parklands (listing opened); a local park. Wikipedia coordinates refer to a Missouri garden of the same name, so the match is wrong.
objection: Counted listing names it.

name: Terowie
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). Historic railway town; the heritage walk and museums (web search) make it a good keep there. Counted source not confirmed.
objection: A historic town with a heritage walk and museums, worth keeping under the Mid North.
